text: Blocks. Stored cross-site scripting in the expense note leaks the user's data to whoever planted the script. Any site the user visits can submit the add form, since it has no forgery protection.
Blocks. The new cell helper reintroduces XSS, which probably breaks every page that lists a tainted category. Both the list and the monthly report route category text through it.
Blocks. My test note with a script tag ran on reload and corrupts the whole expense list view. It fired again every time I opened that month, with no warning on screen.
Should fix. Notes now print as raw page code, so the list probably breaks on any angle bracket. Before this change both note and category were escaped; the shared cell builder dropped that step.
Blocks. Script injection through the category field corrupts the monthly report for anyone who opens it. With no cross-site request check on the forms, a hostile page can plant the payload unseen.
Should fix. A stored note can rewrite what users see and may leak their spending to a stranger. People trust a money app to show their own numbers; a fake page inside it destroys that trust.
Blocks. Category text skips escaping in the shared cell builder, so markup in it reaches the page untouched. The report and the list both call it, so one bad category hits two pages.
Blocks. XSS reproduced on the report page; a script-tag category stops the table rendering and runs instead. Fires on every load of that month's report, in both browsers I tried.
Blocks. Whatever is typed into a note now takes over the tab and leaks everything on it. A hostile website can fill in that note for the user without them ever opening the form.
Should fix. The new cell helper writes note and category raw and skips the old escaping step.
Should fix. Injected markup in a category may break the report and draw a fake prompt over it. Users who trust the page will type whatever it asks for, card numbers included.

Blocks. Opening the expense list can now run someone else's code, which probably leaks every amount and note. The code is stored with the expense, so it fires for the user every time that month loads.
Blocks. The report prints each note as raw page code rather than text, which breaks output encoding. A note with a script tag then runs for anyone viewing the report for that month.
Blocks. This refactor silences the escaping that kept stored XSS out of the list and the report. Worth fixing before release, since the forms also lack any cross-site forgery protection.
Should fix. A test category holding a script tag popped an alert; a real one may delete expenses. Seen on the expense list after saving through the add form, then again after a page refresh.
Optional. Notes now appear without escaping, and I do not know whether that breaks more than the display. A user who pastes angle brackets into a note sees the row change shape, which feels broken.
Blocks. Stored XSS via note and category; the list and report miss the escaping both fields need. A malicious site the user visits can post the add form for them and plant it.
Should fix. A planted note probably corrupts the monthly report, redrawing the totals people rely on. Fires whenever that month's report is opened, and nothing on screen tells the user it happened.
Should fix. Moving list rows onto the new cell builder stops category text from being escaped. Any category with a tag in it now renders as live markup on that row.
Blocks. A booby-trapped expense may run code as the user and quietly delete or rewrite their records. Since the page itself sends the edits, the app cannot tell those changes from the user's own.
Should fix. The CSV export misses formula guarding, so a note starting with equals runs as a formula. It fires when the user opens the export in a spreadsheet program, which most people will do.
Blocks. Exported notes starting with plus, minus, at or equals may leak data when opened in a spreadsheet. The spreadsheet treats them as formulas, and a planted one can call out to another server.
Optional. Export copies each stored note raw and probably corrupts cells whose note reads like a formula. Only bites users who open the file in a spreadsheet program instead of a text editor.

Blocks. The running server overwrites the data file with its in-memory list, which deletes any freshly imported expenses. Fires whenever the import command runs while the server is still up and the next save lands.
Blocks. A month closed while the server runs reappears on its next save and corrupts the archive. Those expenses then sit in both the archive folder and the live file, so totals double count.
Should fix. The server never rereads the data file, so its stale copy may overwrite imported rows. Users are never told to stop the server first, and nothing warns them the data was lost.
Should fix. The month picker only switches months through a script, which blocks users who browse without scripts. There is no submit button to fall back on, so the list stays stuck on one month.

Should fix. Arrowing through the month picker reloads on each keypress and stops keyboard users reaching later months. Tried in the browser with scripts on; with scripts off the picker does nothing at all.

Should fix. Export misses the plan's two-decimal rule, so amounts like 5 or 3.5 come out unpadded. Anyone loading the file into accounting software expecting fixed decimals will see mismatched columns.
Optional. The export writes amounts raw as stored, which probably breaks tools expecting exactly two decimals. A 3.5 expense lands in the export as 3.5 rather than 3.50, as the plan decided.
